authorities.name: Merchant Shipping Act 1995, s.185 and scheduled Limitation Convention Article 4
authorities.citation: Merchant Shipping Act 1995 (c.21) s.185(1); 1976 Limitation Convention Art.4, as scheduled
authorities.court: N/A - primary legislation giving force of law to an international convention
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. The text verified this session is the current in-force version.
authorities.proposition: Section 185(1) gives the Convention on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims 1976 the force of law in the UK. Article 4 of that Convention (Schedule 7, Part I) provides that a person liable shall not be entitled to limit his liability if it is proved that the loss resulted from his personal act or omission, committed with the intent to cause such loss, or recklessly and with knowledge that such loss would probably result - a deliberately narrow gateway, since shipowners' right to limit is otherwise near-automatic.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, on two independent passes, word-for-word consistent both times.

authorities.name: Kairos Shipping Ltd and another v Enka & Co LLC and others (The Atlantik Confidence)
authorities.court: High Court (Queen's Bench Division, Admiralty Court)
authorities.proposition: Article 4's bar on limiting liability requires proof, on a very heavy burden resting on the party challenging the right to limit, that the loss resulted from the shipowner's own personal act or omission done with intent to cause the loss or recklessly with knowledge it would probably result. On the facts, the vessel was found to have been deliberately sunk by the master and chief engineer at the request of the person who was the alter ego of the corporate Owners - satisfying Article 4's test and barring the Owners' claim for a limitation decree. This is the leading English case in which Article 4 has actually been made out at trial, considered rare precisely because the bar is designed to be very difficult to clear.

Paragraph 317's operative deliberate-scuttling holding rests on three independent secondary sources (a law-firm update, the BDM Law blog, and a WebSearch synthesis of multiple firms' commentary) that all reproduce an identical direct quotation - recorded at VERIFIED_SECONDARY_SOURCE per this repository's established practice for cases where every primary-source route is blocked, absent, or unreliable.
